findings.reason: The protected JavaScript solution implements function throttling with leading execution and latest-only trailing execution using state flags (waiting, pending) and setTimeout. The first call executes fn immediately and sets a timer for interval t. Calls during waiting store latest context and args in pending; when timer fires, if pending exists, fn is invoked with pending args and a new timer is scheduled. The solution runs in O(1) time per call and O(1) space; no candidate is required.

Clearing pending before invoking fn ensures reentrant calls are not erased. Starting a new timer interval upon executing a trailing call satisfies the requirement that trailing executions begin a full new window.
Each invocation and timer callback executes in O(1) time and maintains O(1) auxiliary closure state. Complexity evidence is certified and hash-bound.
Accepts function fn and throttle interval t, returning a throttled function with immediate leading and latest-only trailing execution semantics.

The approach accurately details closure state (waiting, pending), leading call execution, timer callback release logic, receiver forwarding, and O(1) time / O(1) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover dropping blocked calls, queuing blocked calls, empty argument arrays, trailing execution interval resets, and receiver preservation.
